title: Why Does the Moon Look Huge on the Horizon?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does the Moon look huge on the horizon?
It isn't bigger. A small pebble at arm's length covers it, high or low.
Measured, it spans about half a degree, wherever it is.
On the horizon it's actually a little farther from you, so a touch smaller.
The difference happens in your brain.
One leading idea: we sense the sky as a flattened dome, so the horizon feels farther away than overhead.
Same size in your eye, but farther away? Then it must be bigger. So your brain blows it up.
Scientists still argue about the full answer.
But the pebble stays the same.
